name: Jira
tagline: Issue and project tracking for software teams, with workflows, sprints, and JQL.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A personal issue tracker is one of the most boring CRUD apps in existence, and an agent will produce a working one in an afternoon: issues, statuses, a drag board, sprints, labels, a search box. If you are a solo developer who uses Jira as an expensive todo list, you lose almost nothing. What you cannot one-shot is the reason Jira actually exists: permission schemes, workflow validators and transition conditions, cross-project reporting, automation rules, and the fact that your PM, QA lead, and three contractors already have the mobile app installed. JQL is a real query language with fifteen years of operators bolted onto it, and reimplementing even 20 percent of it is its own project. Build it for yourself, not for a team of nine.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you create issues with status, type, priority, assignee, labels, and estimate, drag them across a Kanban board, group them into sprints, and filter with a small saved-query language.
requirements: Optional: a GitHub personal access token in .env if you want branch and commit linking
whatYouLose: Permission schemes, issue security levels, and anything resembling multi-team access control
Workflow configuration: transition conditions, validators, post functions, and the approval gates your org quietly depends on
JQL as it actually exists, plus dashboards, burndown, velocity, and cross-project reporting
Native mobile apps, email-to-issue, and notification routing your teammates already expect
The Atlassian integration surface: Confluence, Bitbucket, Slack, Opsgenie, and roughly every CI tool on earth
moatNotes: Nobody chooses Jira because it is pleasant. They choose it because the compliance auditor, the release process, and 40 other seats already live there.
whyPeopleStillPay: Jira is priced per seat and bought by organizations, not individuals, and the purchase is almost never about the board UI. It is about having one system of record that survives reorgs, that auditors accept, that ties to Confluence pages and Bitbucket branches, and that a new hire already knows how to use. Migrating off means rewriting every automation rule, every saved filter someone built in 2019, and every integration that posts status back into a ticket. For a solo user that moat is irrelevant and the free tier covers them anyway. For a company of 50 the moat is the entire product.
notes: Solo, the clone wins easily. The moment a second human needs an opinion about workflow states, you have started rebuilding Jira badly.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user issue tracker called "Tracker" in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/tracker.db, created and migrated on first boot
- No auth, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no external API calls

Data model:
- projects: id, key (e.g. "API"), name, created_at
- issues: id, project_id, seq (per-project counter so keys read API-1, API-2), title, description (markdown), type (task | bug | story | epic), status (backlog | todo | in_progress | review | done), priority (low | medium | high | urgent), assignee (free text), estimate (number or null), parent_id (nullable, for subtasks), sprint_id (nullable), created_at, updated_at
- sprints: id, project_id, name, goal, starts_on, ends_on, state (planned | active | closed)
- comments: id, issue_id, body, created_at
- activity: id, issue_id, field, old_value, new_value, created_at (written on every field change)

Features that are in scope:
- Board view: columns by status, drag and drop to change status, optimistic update then persist
- Backlog view: flat list with inline editing, multi-select, bulk move to sprint
- Issue detail page at /browse/API-1 with markdown description, comments, and an activity log
- Keyboard: "c" creates an issue, "/" focuses search, "e" edits the focused issue
- A tiny query language in the search box supporting: status:, type:, assignee:, priority:, sprint:, text search, and AND only. Parse it with a small hand-written tokenizer, do not pull in a parser library. Saved queries stored in SQLite.
- Export every project to JSON from a button, and a CLI script "npm run export"

Explicitly out of scope, do not build these:
- Permission schemes, roles, multiple users, invites, email
- Custom field builders and configurable workflows: statuses are the fixed enum above
- Burndown charts, velocity, dashboards, gadgets
- Any Atlassian import or API compatibility

Seed the database with one project and about 25 realistic issues across all statuses so the board is not empty on first run.
Ship a README with setup in three commands and a one-paragraph statement of what this deliberately does not do.
